defects.expected: A string set in quotation marks and presented as a user command must appear verbatim in a cited material item. M71 supplies "forget that" verbatim ([0293] lists it among the example forget commands). The delayed-forget limitation is carried by M22/M23 (claim text) and M73 ([0057]) as description, not as quoted speech.
defects.observed: "forget this after three months" is set in quotation marks alongside the genuinely verbatim "forget that", but that string appears in no cited item. M73 reads "The user can instruct the machine-learned agent system to forget information after three months" -- descriptive prose, not a quoted utterance. M71's quoted command list contains only "forget that," "delete this conversation," and "forget information related to [topic]." The substance (forgetting after a stated interval) is grounded in M22/M23/M73; the quotation form attributes to the source a user utterance the source does not contain, and the parallel construction with the adjacent verbatim quote asserts that both came from the disclosure.

defects.expected: A sentence carrying [M116] asserts only what M116 contains. M116 is a positioning item recording the specification's own framing: background_problem, asserted_effect (explicitly "The specification asserts that..."), and the delta "No performance numbers are given; the claimed difference is structural". A proposition that no material item can settle self-declares as [narrative] rather than moving under a material citation.
defects.observed: "That is a described architecture, not a slogan." carries [M116], but its operative clause is an evaluative verdict answering the T1 hook's "architecture or marketing?". No item in the frozen material speaks to marketing or slogans, and M116 records what the specification asserts rather than confirming it. The grounded half -- that an architecture is described -- is already carried by T8 sentences 1 and 2 (M116 delta, plus M3/M12/M19/M21/M40); the added judgment is grounding-free content moving under a material citation instead of a [narrative] self-declaration.

narrative_audit.observation: [narrative]-tagged rhetorical question: "When an AI agent says it 'remembers' you, is that architecture or marketing?" No technical claim about the disclosure. The dichotomy is posed, not resolved, and the presupposition (that agents say they remember users) is about products in general, with no contact point in the frozen material -- there is nothing here to compare against a material item. Recorded because the dichotomy this sentence opens is the one closed at T8 sentence 3 under a material citation, where the grounding obligation does apply; see the defect at that locus.
[narrative]-tagged reader guidance: "Follow along for the next patent walk-through." Pure call to action. No technical claim, no assertion about the patent, no material contact point. Clean.

Surfaced by the narrative audit run in the reverse direction -- not a [narrative]-tagged sentence carrying a technical claim, but grounding-free evaluative content carrying a material citation. Recorded as a defect at this locus (l1.narrative-smuggling); listed here so the audit's coverage of both directions is legible.

observations: T1 sentence 2 opens with "Agents forget, so you re-enter the same details" in the unqualified indicative. The content is back-referenceable -- M116's background_problem reads "Agents without memory force users to re-enter the same details across sessions" -- but that field records the specification's own framing of the prior art, and the clause presents it as ambient fact. The second clause of the same sentence attributes properly ("the claim is a loop"). Not recorded as a defect, since the proposition is present in the cited item. Noted because the same conversion of a spec assertion into a flat statement is what the T8 sentence 3 defect turns on.

T5 sentence 1 compresses two claim paths. CL-19 (M42) matches a portion of the input data to a prior memory object, which the sentence renders directly. CL-18 (M39) matches a current memory object -- created from the input per M38 -- to the prior object, and M38 is not in the citation set {M37,M39,M40,M41,M42,M43,M90,M91,M93,M94}. Each asserted step is back-referenceable, so no defect is recorded; with M38 elided, the "replaced" branch reads as though the input itself displaces the stored object.

T8 sentence 2's "deleted when you ask" splits across two items: the deletion is M21, but the user request is M20, which is not in this sentence's citation set {M3,M12,M19,M21,M40}. M21 carries the request only through its antecedent "the specified information", and T6 sentence 1 cites M20 explicitly. Reported for the record, not as a defect.

Figure-note citation is inconsistent across tweets. T2, T3, T4 and T6 each cite the figure note for their declared figure (M118; M121 and M120; M119; M122). T1, T7 and T8 declare fig: fig-01 but never cite M117, the FIG-1 note, and T5 declares fig: fig-21 but never cites M125. Whether a declared figure must be cited by a sentence is a figure-attachment question rather than sentence-to-material coherence, so it is outside this lane's judgment.

Two items this thread relies on carry open review_requests in the frozen material. M66 (cited at T3 sentence 1) is flagged because [0088] describes extraction as predicting an excerpt to remember rather than in the claim's wording, with [0439] proposed as possibly closer. CL-4 and CL-11 -- the claim texts behind M12 (T4 sentence 1, T8 sentence 2) and M24 (T4 sentence 2) -- are flagged for missing antecedent basis, since "the one or more memory values" and "the plurality of memory objects" have no antecedent in CL-1.
